subject: Flow throttle observed on streaming endpoints — customer advisory & mitigation checklist
body:
From: Jamie Park <jamie.park@fastretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live chat sessions slow / partial streaming stalls

Hi Karthik,

Over the past hour we've seen an uptick in user complaints: live chat responses are arriving in big chunks instead of a steady stream (users report pauses of ~3-6s during replies). This started ~08:40 PT and affects ~12% of active sessions in our us-west region. We pushed a quick retry at the client but it merely reconnected and resumed; however session continuity is important for our agents.

Attached: small trace from one session and a sample client websocket log.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is seeing any streaming-related throttling or capacity routing events? FastRetail has a holiday promotion starting tonight, so time is sensitive.

Thanks,
Jamie
Customer Success Manager
FastRetail

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@fastretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live chat sessions slow / partial streaming stalls

Jamie — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We’re looking into this immediately. Quick notes up front:
- We see elevated queue times on a subset of streaming workers in us-west-2 during the same window.
- Root cause appears related to short-lived backpressure on the real-time KV cache layer which led to delayed token emission in streaming responses.

Short-term we recommend the client-side mitigations below while we triage and apply fixes from our side. I’ll keep this thread updated with timeline estimates.

Immediate mitigation checklist (client):
1) Fallback to non-stream generation for critical agent sessions: set stream=false for sessions where agent continuity matters.
2) Reduce max_tokens on initial requests by 20% to reduce tail latency.
3) Increase websocket ping/keepalive to 30s and implement fast reconnect logic that re-attaches context via conversation_id.
4) If using chunked UI, show a "partial reply" placeholder and allow agent edits to avoid waiting for final chunk.

We’ll share a temporary server-side config to reduce batching latency and push a targeted worker restart to clear misbehaving KV cache instances.

—Karthik
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Live chat sessions slow / partial streaming stalls

Adding telemetry notes and ops action items:
- Telemetry: increased token-emit latency spikes coincident with elevated retries to model endpoint pool m-rt-08.
- Hypothesis: a spike in long-context requests triggered a cascade: larger KV cache lookups slowed downstream streaming loops, causing the worker to fall back to larger batches and then hit the concurrency throttle.

Short term ops actions (executing now):
- Push a targeted 1-node restart on the affected worker shard (us-west-2 / shard-17) to clear stale cache entries. (ETA 8 minutes)
- Temporarily lower the continuous-batch threshold from 40ms -> 12ms for streaming routes serving FastRetail traffic (ETA 20 minutes).
- Route FastRetail traffic to the adjacent pool m-rt-06 for new sessions while we verify stability.

I attached the connection traces we pulled from the edge proxies.

- Ben
Senior SRE, Inference Runtime

Attachment: connection-trace-logs-0903.txt

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@fastretail.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 10:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live chat sessions slow / partial streaming stalls

Jamie — small update: we’ve completed the targeted restart and lowered the batch threshold. Early indicators: token emission tail latency for FastRetail sessions dropped from 450ms p95 to ~120ms p95 across samples. Connectivity errors have not reoccurred in the last 10 minutes for routed sessions.

Please try the following in your staging environment first, then roll to production if it looks good:
- For high-priority agent sessions, toggle stream=false in the payload for the next 30–60 minutes while we monitor.
- If you prefer to keep streaming enabled, add the client-side keepalive change (30s) and set max_tokens to -20% for the next 2 hrs.

We will keep the routing fallback in place for 60 minutes and then slowly shift sessions back to m-rt-08 once we confirm KV cache behavior is stable.

Attachment: recommended-params-0903.pdf

—Marissa
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
From: Jamie Park <jamie.park@fastretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live chat sessions slow / partial streaming stalls

Thanks everyone — we applied the client-side keepalive and reduced max_tokens as recommended. Initial telemetry looks promising: the number of reported pauses dropped to <1% during the 14:20–15:00 window. We’ll keep monitoring through tonight’s promotion window and will escalate if anything reoccurs.

A couple of follow-ups for your post-incident summary:
- Can you confirm root cause once the postmortem is ready (KV cache eviction/lookup pattern + batching logic)?
- Any recommended longer-term configuration (e.g., model-routing policy, reduced batch thresholds during promotions) to prevent recurrence?

We appreciate the quick response.

Jamie
Customer Success Manager
FastRetail
